target_customer: Online marketplaces and crowdfunding platforms that need to collect and pay out money between buyers and sellers
problem: Marketplaces had to build escrow, split payments and seller payouts themselves or use PayPal Adaptive Payments with stacked fees. Balanced offered a white-label payments API for marketplaces.
business_model: Payments API with processing fees per transaction

founders.name: Matin Tamizi
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CEO who announced the shutdown (TechCrunch 2015). The YC page lists no founders.

founders.name: Jareau Wade
founders.background_notes: Described as Balanced founder in a VentureBeat headline.

exit.reason: Company said it failed to achieve the growth needed to continue independently; Stripe took over its roughly 320 customers in a transition deal and Balanced closed June 11, 2015

competitors.name: PayPal Adaptive Payments
competitors.what: API that split a payment across several recipients, used by marketplaces
competitors.traction_then: Available with a 2011 user manual; marketplace fees stacked on each leg

technical_complexity.rationale: Payments needed bank and card processing integration, escrow, compliance and fraud controls, which is heavy for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Marketplaces embedded the API and stored seller data, but Stripe and Braintree could and did add marketplace features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: As Stripe expanded services to compete more directly, Balanced's customer numbers waned and it closed in 2015, handing customers to Stripe.

market_need_then: Marketplaces such as crowdfunding and peer to peer sites needed split payments and escrow; PayPal's option stacked fees.

branding.domain_note: Used balancedpayments.com rather than the exact .com
branding.community_and_virality: Founder framed it as an alternative to Braintree and Stripe in VentureBeat; no merch or fan community found

brand_strength.rationale: Known in the developer payments niche but a generic word name with a payments suffix domain and no brand assets found.

outcome_analysis: Balanced raised 3.4 million dollars of seed money including Andreessen Horowitz, but Stripe broadened into marketplace payments and Balanced's customer count shrank, so in March 2015 it announced a 90 day wind down and moved about 320 clients to Stripe. The company cited a failure to grow fast enough. No Series A was found.
notes: Total raised: TechCrunch and YC blog say 3.4 million seed; CB Insights lists 4.2 million, unreconciled. The 2012-11 date of the first round is inferred from the article saying the lead round was the previous November, so treat the year as probable. Rebrand from PoundPay rests on trademark records and a search summary, not an opened source. YC page lists no founders; names come from press. balancedpayments.com returned HTTP 403. Competitor Stripe not listed because no source dated near 2011 was opened.
